description: Recorded measurements that back an evidence claim. A capability value cites one as 'measurement:<id>' in its evidence mapping, the same way it cites 'make:<target>' or 'example:<case>'. The difference is what the source is: a make target or example is re-runnable on demand, while a measurement is a run that already happened and cannot be cheaply repeated - a cluster campaign, a refinement study, a reference comparison. Recording it here is what lets a later reader, human or agent, see that the question was already answered, on what, and to what threshold, instead of running it again.

record_contract.id: stable identifier, referenced as measurement:<id> and cited by name in the capability entry
record_contract.question: the single question the campaign was run to answer
record_contract.date: ISO date the measurement was taken
record_contract.commit: repository revision the measurement was taken at
record_contract.environment: machine, scheduler, and rank layout the run actually used
record_contract.configuration: case, grid, and the settings that determine the result
record_contract.result: what was measured, the threshold it was judged against, and the verdict: met, not-met, or inconclusive
record_contract.limitations: what this measurement does not establish; required, and 'none' is not an acceptable value
record_contract.artifacts: committed derived data supporting the result; may be empty when the numbers in 'result' are the whole record
